name: Gaina
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: SIL reapdata file '' (CDX hit on '_gcn') -- turned out to be Ministerio de Educacion / ILV 1982, Non Paron Ja Jahuequibo, Shipibo-Conibo science primer (Peru)
sources.note: False hit, not Gaina; scanned of pp.1-5 identified it; file deleted from the gain1243 folder and noted

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1971. Languages of South-East Papua: a preliminary report. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 1-46. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Locates Gaina (Iwuji village) and gives lexicostatistical percentages (60-74% with Notu, 52-58% with Baruga); the word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the volume.

sources.citation: Smallhorn, Jacinta Mary. 2011. The Binanderean languages of Papua New Guinea: reconstruction and subgrouping. Pacific Linguistics 625. Canberra: ANU. xvi+466 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 3.6 'Suprasegmentals' pp.79-80 (PDF 95-96): no statement about Gaena stress. Says phonemic stress with low functional load is reported for Yekora, Baruga, Korafe; and (p.80) 'In the case of Proto Binandere, penultimate stress is assumed for two- and three-syllable words (at least in the case of non-verbs), based on the analyses of stress in the present-day languages; Suena, Zia, Binandere, Hunjara, Tafota Baruga, and Korafe all exhibit this pattern.' -- Gaena is not among the languages named. Source table p.15 (PDF 31) shows Gaena is documented only by wordlists (Dutton 1968 ~220 words;…

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. [2010]. Gaina Swadesh List. archive.org item rosettaproject_gcn_swadesh-1 (11 items, no source named).
sources.note: 11 body-part words without stress marking; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: transnewguinea.org language page 'Gaina' (lexibank; sources McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970, Smallhorn 2011, Wilson 1969)
sources.note: Lexical items only; no phonology notes.

sources.citation: Wilson, Darryl. 1969. The Binandere language family. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 9 (Pacific Linguistics A-18), 65-86. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 3.1 Phonology pp.68-69 is 'based mainly on the six northern members'; only remark touching prosody is that Suena tone 'is separate from stress and may well be phonemic'. Gaina appears only in the village list (Iwuji) and a short wordlist; nothing on Gaina stress.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG language resources for Gaina [gcn] (pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/search/code/gcn; www.sil.org/resources/search/language/gcn) -- to check whether an Organised Phonology Data sheet, alphabet-design worksheet or sociolinguistic survey report exists for Gaina (the Farrs' Korafe/Baruga team worked with the neighbouring Gaina/Karoto villages).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: An SIL OPD sheet, if one exists, would carry an explicit 'Stress' paragraph as the Baruga (Farr & Farr 2005) and Korafe ones do; could not verify existence because both SIL sites and OLAC were unreachable.

sources.citation: Farr, Cynthia. 2001. Karoto-English dictionary (c. 400 entries). Unpublished computer file, SIL Ukarumpa (Smallhorn's source CF01; Karoto = Karajembo, assigned to Gaena).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Compiled by the Korafe specialist; SIL Toolbox dictionaries of this team mark stress (cf. Korafe F&F90 forms in Smallhorn) and front matter may state the stress rule for the Gaina/Karoto lect.

sources.citation: Parrington, Douglas & Margaret Parrington. 1984. [Wordlists of Notu, Oukena (Yega), Karajembo, Gena and Gaena, 100 entries each, with location notes pp.3-4]. Unpublished ms, SIL Ukarumpa (Smallhorn's source P&P84).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Three Gaena-area lists by the Notu (Ewage) SIL team; may include transcription notes on stress, though Smallhorn (p.24) rates its phonetics as coarse.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1968. Field wordlists, South-East Papua survey: Gaina (Iwuji, ~220 words) and 'Notu?' [= Gena] (~120 words), stress-marked phonetic transcription (Smallhorn's source TD68). Unpublished; probably in PARADISEC collection TD1 or ANU archives.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only first-hand phonetic record of Gaina with stress marked on every item; a header note or Dutton's transcription conventions may state the default stress; would let the penult pattern be cited from the primary rather than via Smallhorn's appendix.
